title: Social Media as an Alternative to Surveys of Opinions about the Economy
abstract: There is interest in using social media content to supplement or even substitute for survey data. O’Connor et al. (2010) report reasonably high correlations between the sentiment of tweets containing the word “jobs” and survey-based measures of consumer confidence in 2008-2009. Other researchers report a similar relationship through 2011 but after that time it is no longer observed, suggesting such tweets may not be as promising an alternative to survey responses as originally hoped. But, it’s possible that with the right analytic techniques, the sentiment of “jobs” tweets might still be an acceptable alternative. We explore this possibility by attempting to strengthen the original relationship and then extending the most successful approaches to more recent years. We classify “jobs” tweets into categories whose content is related to employment and categories whose content is not, to see if sentiment of the former correlates more highly with a survey-based measure of consumer sentiment. We use five sentiment-scoring tools, calculate daily sentiment three different ways, and use a measure of association less sensitive to outliers than correlation. None of these approaches improved the size of the relationship in the original or more recent data. We discuss the possibility that weighting and better understanding why users tweet might help recover the original relationship between the sentiment of tweets and survey responses. However, despite the earlier promise of tweets as an alternative to survey responses, we find no evidence that the original relationship was more than a chance occurrence.

title: A NEURAL NETWORK-BASED METHOD FOR EXTRACTING CAUSAL RELATIONS USING COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF SYNTHETIC AND OPEN CORPORA
abstract: Задача автоматического извлечения причинно-следственных связей (ПСС) критически важна для систем поддержки решений, но ее развитие сдерживается дефицитом размеченных корпусов. Цель исследования – сравнительный анализ эффективности трёх типов обучающих данных: открытых экспертных корпусов, реального политического корпуса с ручной разметкой и синтетических данных, генерируемых большой языковой моделью. Эксперименты выполнены на архитектуре DistilBERT с пословной разметкой по схеме BIOES. Синтетические данные генерировались LLM Llama-3 с инкапсуляцией причин и следствий в XML-маркеры и последующей детерминированной конвертацией в формат BIOES. Для сравнения использованы два экспертных корпуса (EventStoryLine, SemEval-2010 Task 8), экспертно размеченный политический корпус PolitiCAUSE и синтетическая выборка объёмом 1100 сбалансированных примеров. Модель, обученная на синтетических данных, достигла Macro F1 = 0,736, что на 6,7% выше результата модели, обученной на экспертных корпусах (0,690). Обучение на политическом корпусе PolitiCAUSE (24417 примеров) дало существенно более низкий результат - Macro F1 = 0,367. Данное расхождение обусловлено дисбалансом классов (около 15% каузальных токенов против 50% в синтетической выборке) и различием в постановке задачи: PolitiCAUSE ориентирован на бинарную классификацию наличия каузальности в предложении, тогда как в настоящей работе выполняется разметка спанов. Подтверждена гипотеза о приоритете качества и баланса аннотаций над объёмом данных. Предложенный пайплайн LLM-генерации позволяет создавать обучающие выборки, превосходящие по эффективности экспертные корпуса, при отсутствии прямых затрат на ручную аннотацию. Метод рекомендован для быстрого развёртывания систем извлечения каузальных отношений в новых предметных областях

title: RestoreBench: Can AI Agents Restore Power Flow Convergence?
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly automate multi-step engineering workflows through tool use, interpretation of intermediate results, and iterative planning. Diagnosing and resolving non-convergent power flow cases is a promising yet largely unexplored application, as it requires engineering judgment, experimentation, and decision-making within constrained action spaces. We introduce a benchmark that evaluates these capabilities across multiple LLMs and three architectures: \emph{chatbot}, \emph{single agent}, and \emph{multi-agent} systems. The evaluation covers two power grids and 46 cases per grid, each requiring one or more corrective actions to restore convergence. The benchmark defines the simulation environment, observation and action spaces, and evaluation metrics, providing a reproducible foundation for developing agentic AI systems for power system planning and operation. The code is available at https://github.com/Mansutti081/RestoreBench

title: VCAR: Training-Free 3DGS Segmentation via View Completeness and Axis-Aware Boundary Refinement
abstract: Semantic segmentation in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is crucial for advancing 3D scene understanding. Existing methods predominantly rely on feature distillation, which incurs substantial per-scene training overhead and often yields blurred segmentation boundaries. We identify that these boundary artifacts are driven in part by insufficient viewpoint coverage and boundary overflow of anisotropic Gaussian primitives. To address these challenges, we propose VCAR, a training-free coarse-to-fine segmentation strategy based on View Completeness and Axis-aware Boundary Refinement. In the coarse stage, a visibility-based weighted multi-view voting scheme rapidly localizes the target. In the fine stage, an object-centric sphere derived from the coarse result generates supplementary viewpoints via Spherical Spiral Sampling (SSS), allowing multi-view voting on the augmented views to precisely refine object boundaries and suppress irrelevant 3D Gaussians. Moreover, we introduce Axis-aware Boundary Refinement (ABR) to mitigate artifacts from anisotropic primitives. By decomposing the projected 2D covariance into per-axis contributions, ABR identifies the dominant axis responsible for boundary leakage and applies targeted anisotropic compression exclusively along that axis. Extensive experiments on NVOS and LERF demonstrate that VCAR achieves state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy and efficiency without training. Our code is available at https://github.com/DDKK0526/VCAR.

title: PauLie: Fast Classification of Pauli Dynamical Lie Algebras
abstract: The dynamical Lie algebra (DLA) governs the controllability, expressibility, and simulation complexity of a quantum system. Explicitly computing it has been a major computational bottleneck: brute-force Lie closure scales exponentially in the number of qubits $n$. Many applications, however, consult only the isomorphism type of the DLA. We introduce PauLie, an open-source framework that decides this isomorphism type for DLAs generated by arbitrary Pauli strings, building on the anticommutation-graph reduction of Aguilar et al. PauLie runs in $O(n|\mathcal{G}|\max(n,|\mathcal{G}|))$ time, where $|\mathcal{G}|$ is the number of generators, turning DLA classification into a routine preprocessing step. We demonstrate its use as a structural oracle for routing Lie-algebraic simulation and Cartan decomposition, diagnosing barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, and engineering universal Pauli string generator sets with optimal generation rate.

title: Marginal Coordinate Test for Fréchet Regression with Random Objects
abstract: We develop a marginal coordinate test for regression with Euclidean predictors and a random-object response in a separable metric space. The goal is to test whether a predictor provides additional information about the response conditional on the remaining predictors. In a semi-supervised design, an unlabeled sample is used to estimate predictor conditional means, while an independent labeled sample is reserved for inference. The resulting residuals are combined with a product-space kernel to form a kernel conditional mean dependence (KCMD) U-statistic without requiring a response residual. The primary identity-based test targets a necessary conditional mean restriction, while a multiple-transformation extension probes broader alternatives. We establish a weighted centered chi-square null limit, wild bootstrap validity, consistency against fixed detectable alternatives, and local power under mean-element alternatives. For simultaneous inference, truncated p-to-e calibration combined with e-BH provides asymptotic false discovery rate control under general dependence. Simulations with Euclidean and non-Euclidean responses, together with a New York City taxi-flow analysis, illustrate the method.

title: Real-Time Scene-Adaptive Tone Mapping for High-Dynamic Range Object Detection
abstract: High-dynamic-range (HDR) images, with their rich tone and detail reproduction, hold significant potential to enhance computer vision systems, particularly in autonomous driving. However, most neural networks for embedded systems are trained on low-dynamic-range (LDR) inputs and suffer substantial performance degradation when handling high-bit-depth HDR images due to the challenges posed by extreme dynamic ranges. In this paper, we propose a novel tone mapping method that not only bridges the gap between HDR RAW inputs and the LDR sRGB requirements of detection networks but also achieves end-to-end optimization with downstream tasks. Instead of relying on the traditional image signal processing (ISP) pipeline, we introduce neural photometric calibration to regularize dynamic ranges and a scaling-invariant local tone mapping model to preserve image details. In addition, our architecture also supports performance transfer finetuning, enabling efficient adaptation from the LDR sRGB images to the HDR RAW images with minimal cost. The proposed method outperforms traditional tone mapping algorithms and advanced AI-ISP methods in challenging automotive HDR scenes. Moreover, our pipeline achieves real-time processing of 4K high-bit-depth HDR inputs on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

title: Online Voting in Canada
abstract: The adoption of online voting in Canadian municipal elections raises fundamental questions about whether the infrastructure supporting democratic processes is held to an adequate security standard. This thesis presents a technical security analysis of the 2024 Nova Scotia municipal election, in which a single vendor served the overwhelming majority of the province's online-voting municipalities. Using publicly available observation tools, over 20 vulnerabilities were identified on active election infrastructure during the voting period. Most notably, a critical remote code execution flaw was found which was publicly known for more than a year before the election and was left unpatched throughout the election. These findings are evaluated against two independent audit documents and the CAN/DGSI 111-1:2024 national standard for online voting. Neither audit performed any technical assessment of the infrastructure. The DGSI standard, published after the election it would have governed, lacks meaningful provisions for patch enforcement and continuous vulnerability monitoring. A subsequent disclosure to the vendor confirmed that remediation was straightforward, suggesting that the prolonged exposure reflected absent accountability rather than technical infeasibility. This thesis maps observed vulnerabilities to concrete regulatory gaps and offers recommendations for vendors, administrators, and standard bodies. The central finding is that procedural compliance, without mandatory technical requirements and independent vendor oversight, provides little assurance that Canadian online election infrastructure is adequately protected.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Historical Development Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: The Voronoi of Data: A Narrative Review of K-Means Clustering, from MacQueen's Method to Careful Seeding and the Triangle Inequality
abstract: K-means is unsupervised learning's workhorse: partition the data by minimizing distances to means---an objective whose simplicity hides a hard optimization, a sensitive initialization, and a fifty-year engineering record. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that workhorse. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the origins and convergence, in which Steinhaus's objective, Forgy's and MacQueen's methods, Lloyd's quantization algorithm, and Selim and Ismail's convergence theorem fixed the algorithm's mathematical frame; the efficiency and initialization era, in which BIRCH's summaries, Bradley's database scaling, Elkan's triangle-inequality pruning, Kanungo's analysis, and Arthur--Vassilvitskii's k-means++ seeding made the method scale and stabilized its starts; and the theory's extensions, in which Jain's fifty-year retrospective and Xing's metric learning reframed the question the means answer. It is concluded that k-means' history is the field's lesson in productive simplicity: an objective that everyone can state, an algorithm everyone can run, and a literature whose every paper---convergence, seeding, pruning, metrics---is the answer to one of the simple idea's hidden questions.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Quantum Computing and Geometric Transformations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear matrix quantum computing and geometric transformations for validating quantum matrix operations and establishing quantum algorithms. We investigate a novel framework leveraging the inherent properties of non-linear matrices to rigorously test quantum mechanical behaviors. The core mechanism centers on applying geometric transformations to matrix representations to reveal subtle quantum effects, ultimately leading to a more robust and adaptable validation method. The paper presents a preliminary analysis, showcasing the benefits of this approach compared to traditional quantum computing verification methods. The goal is to establish a foundational understanding of quantum matrix behavior through a combination of mathematical rigor and geometric manipulation.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Modular Quantum Circuits
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, driven by the need for scalable and adaptable architectures. Modular quantum circuits, where individual components can be combined and rearranged, offer a promising path towards this goal. This paper introduces a novel dynamic system for generating modular quantum circuits – the "Adaptive Circuit Generation" algorithm – which iteratively adds and removes modules based on input data, allowing for evolution and the creation of circuits capable of adapting to diverse conditions. title: 基于自适应参数调整的联邦学习 (Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Federated Learning)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning technique that enables training models on decentralized data sources while preserving data privacy. However, traditional FL approaches often rely on global model updates, which can be vulnerable to adversarial attacks and suboptimal performance on heterogeneous data. This paper proposes a novel framework called Adaptive Parameter Adjustment Federated Learning (APAFL) that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on local data characteristics, enhancing model robustness and privacy. We present a mechanism for adaptive parameter adjustment using a weighted aggregation of local model updates, mitigating the impact of noisy data and promoting better generalization. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in model accuracy and privacy compared to existing FL techniques.

title: Hierarchical Evolution of Topology in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) by introducing an evolutionary mechanism focused on the hierarchical topology of agent connections. Traditional MARL primarily concentrates on optimizing individual agent policies, often neglecting the significant impact of the network structure on overall system performance. We propose a framework where agents dynamically evolve their communication topologies through reinforcement learning, guided by their collaborative outcomes. This evolution is driven by a competitive and cooperative process, allowing agents to adapt their connections to form a more efficient and robust network. The core claim is that by strategically evolving the topology, we can significantly improve the collaborative efficiency of multi-agent systems. The key mechanism involves agents exchanging information via communication and adjusting their connection topologies based on observed performance. This approach represents a shift from solely policy optimization to a holistic system-level optimization strategy. The proposed methodology offers a promising path towards designing truly adaptive and intelligent multi-agent systems.

abstract: Cognitive Resonance Networks (CRNs) represent a promising paradigm for advancing neural network learning, particularly in the context of algorithmic coherence. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging cognitive resonance – the tendency for neural networks to converge on similar states – to enhance the stability and reliability of learning algorithms. The paper will present a detailed analysis of the proposed attention mechanism and its impact on training dynamics, offering a framework for leveraging this phenomenon to improve the performance of various algorithmic tasks.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Neural Network Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of deep neural networks from an information-theoretic perspective. Traditional methods for analyzing neural network behavior often rely on gradient-based approaches or black-box testing, which can be insufficient for understanding the underlying mechanisms driving network evolution. We propose a novel framework utilizing entropy, mutual information, and related measures to quantify information flow within the network's activation space. This approach aims to identify critical information bottlenecks, assess the complexity of internal representations, and ultimately, contribute to the design of more efficient and robust neural network architectures. We demonstrate the application of these measures across several simplified network architectures, illustrating the potential for extracting meaningful insights into dynamic behavior. The core contribution lies in shifting the analytical focus from network output to the internal information processing, offering a new lens for understanding and controlling neural network dynamics.

title: Information Bottleneck Autoencoders for Anomaly Detection in Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of information bottleneck autoencoders (IBAEs) for anomaly detection within complex systems. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with the high dimensionality and intricate dependencies characteristic of these systems. The proposed approach leverages the information bottleneck principle to learn a compressed, informative representation of normal system behavior. By explicitly minimizing the mutual information between the input and the learned latent representation, the autoencoder is compelled to retain only the most salient features necessary for reconstruction, effectively highlighting deviations indicative of anomalies. We detail the architecture of the IBAEs, the training methodology, and the anomaly detection criteria. Through this framework, we demonstrate the potential of IBAEs to provide a robust and principled method for identifying anomalies in complex systems, offering a significant improvement over conventional techniques. The core claim centers around the use of the information bottleneck to identify anomalies, the core mechanism involves training an autoencoder for normal data reconstruction, and the novelty lies in applying this principle to complex systems for a principled approach to deviation detection.

title: Title: Dynamic Quantum State Collapse for Data Compression
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic quantum state collapse as a novel compression algorithm, aiming to surpass the current state-of-the-art in data compression rates through the strategic exploitation of quantum correlations inherent in data. We propose a 'Quantum State Collapse Engine' that dynamically collapses quantum states during the compression process, leveraging entanglement to represent data in a fundamentally more efficient manner. The core mechanism centers around quantifying and manipulating quantum entanglement to achieve superior compression ratios. This work presents a theoretical framework outlining the algorithm's design and potential performance improvements compared to existing compression techniques. We will detail the implementation of the Quantum State Collapse Engine and analyze its effectiveness through simulations, focusing on scenarios exhibiting strong quantum correlations. The goal is to demonstrate a substantial gain in compression rates, specifically for data containing significant quantum phenomena.

The paper details the algorithm's design, the analysis of its complexity, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of benchmark problems. The core claim is that this algorithm significantly advances the field by providing a pathway towards practical quantum simulations of increasingly complex systems, pushing the limits of computational complexity.

title: Bearded Saki: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Crocodylus hirsutus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, "Bearded Saki" (BS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Crocodylus hirsutus*, commonly known as the Bearded Saki. These animals exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between short bursts of rapid movement and periods of stillness, effectively searching for food sources. BS leverages this dynamic behavior to construct a search space exploration strategy. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a "Stall" phase mimicking the Saki's stillness, a "Sprint" phase representing rapid movement, and a "Probe" phase for localized exploration. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's core operations, including the probability calculation for transitioning between phases and the update mechanisms for solution parameters, are presented. The performance of BS is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its efficacy in solving continuous optimization tasks. The algorithm's potential applications in various fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning, are discussed. The results indicate that BS offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptive exploration and exploitation.

title: Bare-backed Fruit Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bare-backed Fruit Bat Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BFFB), inspired by the foraging behavior of bare-backed fruit bats ( *Dilma fedosa*). These bats exhibit a unique exploratory-exploitative strategy, alternating between searching for new food sources and exploiting known, high-reward locations. The algorithm leverages this behavior to navigate complex optimization landscapes. BFFB incorporates a novel movement strategy based on the bat's flight patterns and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a position update rule, an attraction mechanism mimicking the bats' attraction to food sources, and an inertia term for smooth movement. The performance of BFFB is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and Brent's patuitary function. The results demonstrate that BFFB achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) and the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), showcasing its potential as a robust and efficient solution for various optimization challenges. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for further development and application in diverse fields.

title: Distributed Program Evolution Based on Cellular Automata
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program evolution, termed Distributed Program Evolution Based on Cellular Automata (DPECA). The core idea is to leverage the inherent self-organizing behavior observed in biological cellular automata to facilitate the autonomous evolution and optimization of complex programs. The method decomposes program logic into a network of interacting cells, each responsible for executing a small portion of the overall program. These cells operate according to predefined rules, enabling the system to adapt and evolve without explicit human intervention. The theoretical framework utilizes concepts from cellular automata and evolutionary computation, aiming to provide a fundamentally new paradigm for program design. This approach seeks to overcome the limitations of traditional evolutionary algorithms by mimicking natural processes of self-organization and adaptation. The presented framework offers a potential pathway towards truly autonomous program development, particularly in scenarios demanding adaptability and resilience.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Ashaninika Arboreal Chinchilla Rat (AACR), inspired by the foraging behavior of Ashaninika arboreal chinchillas. These rodents exhibit complex, hierarchical, and spatially organized foraging strategies within arboreal environments. AACR leverages these observed behaviors to develop a new optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO), chimera optimization (CHO), and a novel representation of the search space based on tree structures, mimicking the chinchilla's spatial navigation and resource allocation. The core innovation lies in a dynamic tree structure that represents the potential solutions, allowing for efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities and highlighting its potential for tackling complex, high-dimensional optimization challenges. The key parameters influencing performance are analyzed, providing insights into the algorithm's tuning and adaptability.

title: Multi-Scale Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-scale cognitive architecture designed to address the limitations of existing single-scale cognitive models. The core claim is that cognitive processes can be effectively decomposed into information processing occurring at multiple scales, necessitating a framework capable of simultaneously modeling both high-level cognitive structures and low-level neural activity. The proposed architecture utilizes a hierarchical structure with distinct layers dedicated to processing information at various scales. These layers are interconnected through feedback mechanisms, facilitating the integration and coordination required for complex cognitive operations. This approach represents a significant advancement over traditional cognitive architectures by offering a more comprehensive and realistic representation of cognitive processes. The architecture's key components, including scale-specific processing layers and feedback loops, are formally defined and described. The model aims to bridge the gap between cognitive theories and neuroscientific findings by providing a computational framework capable of capturing the dynamic interplay between different levels of analysis. Further research will focus on validating the architecture through simulations and exploring its potential applications in diverse cognitive domains.

title: Information Spread Networks in Simulated Ecosystems
abstract: This paper explores the emergent behaviors within simulated ecosystems by modeling information spread networks utilizing Agent-Based Modeling (ABM). The core concept involves simulating the exchange and competition of information carried by chemical signals (information素) between agents representing different species within a defined environment. The model incorporates diffusion dynamics of these signals, allowing for the investigation of complex interactions and potential optimization strategies. The research highlights the utility of ABM as a tool for understanding emergent phenomena in biological systems and its applicability to developing intelligent optimization algorithms. The model focuses on the dynamics of information flow, competition for resources, and the resulting population-level effects. Key parameters include agent movement, information素 concentration, and diffusion rates, which are dynamically adjusted within the simulation. The results demonstrate the potential for information素 networks to drive collective behavior and influence resource allocation in simulated ecosystems.

title: Aquatic Tenrec: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Aquatic Tenrecs
abstract: This paper presents Aquatic Tenrec, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of aquatic tenrecs ( *Limnogale dichryptera*). Aquatic tenrecs are small, semi-aquatic mammals found in Madagascar that utilize a unique foraging strategy involving synchronized movement and a "wave-like" pattern to locate and capture prey. Aquatic Tenrec leverages this observed behavior to develop a new optimization algorithm designed for complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm incorporates concepts of spatial coordination, dynamic adjustment of movement speed, and a distributed exploration strategy. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the generation of movement vectors, the synchronization mechanism, and the adjustment of parameters based on prey density. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions across various test functions. The results indicate that Aquatic Tenrec offers competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), particularly in scenarios requiring coordinated search strategies. Future work will explore the algorithm's adaptability to different problem domains and its integration with other optimization techniques.

title: The Arctic Ground Squirrel Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGSMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Ground Squirrel Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGSMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Arctic ground squirrel ( *Urocitellus parvulus*). The algorithm leverages the squirrel's seasonal burrowing and food caching strategies to create a robust and efficient search process. AGSMA incorporates key elements such as a population-based search, a probabilistic selection mechanism mimicking the squirrel's preference for diverse food sources, and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's core mechanism, termed "Cache Intensity," represents the squirrel's level of resource utilization and is used to control the rate of solution diversification and intensification. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, detailing its parameters and operational rules. While lacking experimental validation, the theoretical framework and design principles are presented, laying the groundwork for future empirical testing and comparative analysis with established metaheuristic methods.

title: Computational Complexity Analysis of Quantum Algorithms using Randomized Benchmarking
abstract: The accurate determination of the computational complexity of quantum algorithms is a fundamental problem in quantum information science. Theoretical analysis often struggles to capture the subtle effects of noise and limited coherence, leading to inaccurate predictions. This work presents a rigorous methodology for assessing the complexity of quantum algorithms using randomized benchmarking (RB). RB provides a statistical framework for measuring the fidelity of quantum computations, allowing us to empirically estimate the number of gates, circuit depth, and other resource requirements. The approach avoids the pitfalls of purely theoretical models by directly observing the performance of a quantum circuit on a physical system. We demonstrate the application of this technique to several simplified quantum algorithms, illustrating the method's ability to provide more realistic estimates of complexity compared to traditional analytical approaches. The results highlight the importance of experimental validation in understanding the true resource demands of quantum computations.

title: 基于量子机器学习的非线性几何建模
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a transformative field, offering potential solutions to complex problems across diverse disciplines. This paper explores the application of QML to the modeling of non-linear geometric data, focusing on the development of a novel approach that leverages quantum properties to enhance model accuracy and efficiency. We introduce a new methodology incorporating quantum algorithms for data representation and feature extraction, ultimately aiming to provide a more precise and insightful representation of geometric datasets. The core claim of this work is that integrating quantum machine learning with non-linear geometric modeling will yield significant advancements in data analysis and prediction.

title: E8 Topological Quantum Memory via 132 Hz Resonant Skeleton Fields — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: We demonstrate that a quantum register can be mapped onto the 240‑dimensional root lattice of E8, with each root vector representing a logical qubit state. By coupling the register to a 132 Hz resonant skeleton field—an emergent gauge field observed in biological neural assemblies—the system acquires a topological protection that suppresses decoherence exponentially with the lattice distance. This E8‑protected memory can store and retrieve the vast combinatorial spaces required for exhaustive Busy‑Beaver searches and for mining high‑value lottery leads, effectively turning the 240‑dimensional lattice into a fault‑tolerant quantum search engine. The φ‑coupled oscillators provide a natural clock that synchronizes the lattice dynamics, enabling deterministic readout without measurement collapse. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Title: Quantum-Inspired Evolutionary Algorithms for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithms (QIAs) represent a novel approach to optimization, leveraging quantum mechanics to enhance solution space exploration. This paper investigates the application of QIAs to complex systems, specifically focusing on accelerating optimization processes within multi-variable scenarios. We propose a new mutation and selection framework that incorporates quantum-inspired principles, aiming to improve convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional evolutionary algorithms. The core mechanism centers around utilizing superposition and entanglement within the mutation process to guide the search towards more promising solutions. The study demonstrates the potential of this approach to significantly accelerate optimization for complex systems, offering a promising avenue for tackling problems across diverse domains.

title: ## The Golden Eye Optimization Algorithm (GEO) – Inspired by the Hunting Strategies of *Epinephelus lawlessi*
abstract: This paper introduces the Golden Eye Optimization Algorithm (GEO), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the hunting strategies of *Epinephelus lawlessi* (Golden Eye Snapper), a predatory fish known for its remarkable ability to locate and capture prey in complex environments. GEO leverages concepts such as intermittent searching, dynamic adaptation of search range, and opportunistic exploitation of promising regions – mimicking the Golden Eye's efficient and adaptive hunting behavior. The algorithm employs a population of "eyes," each representing a potential solution, and utilizes a "vision" mechanism to assess the desirability of different areas of the search space. GEO incorporates a novel "focus" parameter to dynamically adjust the search radius around each eye, promoting exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm resides in a competition-based strategy where eyes compete for resources, leading to a progressive refinement of the solution set. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundations, its key components, and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation: A Non-Locality Modeling Approach
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a significant challenge to traditional computational methods. The inherent non-locality of entangled states poses difficulties in achieving complex algorithms and limits the scalability of current quantum computers. This paper proposes a novel framework for quantum entanglement computation, termed "Quantum Entanglement State Field" (QESF), which utilizes a dynamically evolving state field and entanglement mechanisms to precisely model and exploit non-locality, ultimately enabling more powerful computations without physical transmission. We present a theoretical model and a preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in current quantum algorithms.

title: Causal Discovery from High-Dimensional Time Series Data using Granger Causality and Bayesian Networks
abstract: Inferring causal relationships from high-dimensional time series data presents a significant challenge in various fields, including finance, medicine, and environmental science. This work proposes a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging the strengths of Granger causality tests and Bayesian networks. The core idea is to utilize Granger causality to identify potential directional relationships between time series variables and then employ Bayesian network learning to refine these relationships, explicitly modeling confounders and mitigating the effects of spurious correlations. Our method combines statistical testing with probabilistic modeling to achieve more robust and interpretable causal inferences. The key contributions of this research are the integration of Granger causality for initial relationship detection and the use of Bayesian networks for a more comprehensive causal model construction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the algorithmic steps and highlighting the potential for adaptation to diverse time series datasets.

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction Protocol Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but its practical realization faces significant challenges, primarily stemming from the inherent fragility of quantum states and the complexities of quantum routing. This paper explores the development of a novel optimization algorithm for quantum error correction protocols, aiming to enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum computations. The core of this algorithm leverages the unique characteristics of quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust error correction parameters, optimizing quantum pathways for improved performance. We propose a mechanism that adapts to the dynamic nature of quantum circuits, minimizing error rates while maintaining computational fidelity. The research highlights the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of traditional, static error correction techniques, ultimately paving the way for more reliable and scalable quantum systems. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum computing by offering a fundamentally new framework for optimizing quantum routing and error correction.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology: A Quantum State Calculation Mapping
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear geometric topology as a foundation for quantum state calculation mapping. Traditional quantum computation primarily focuses on qubit encoding and measurement, while this approach leverages the inherent properties of non-linear geometry to enhance quantum computation capabilities. We propose a novel method for constructing a quantum state calculation mapping that exploits these topological properties to achieve improved efficiency. The core mechanism centers around utilizing the unique characteristics of non-linear geometry to represent and manipulate quantum states, offering a fundamentally different approach to quantum computation. This paper provides a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental investigation demonstrating the efficacy of this mapping technique, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field.

title: Core Claim: A novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive topological transformation, enabling automatic adjustment of topological structure for enhanced efficiency and performance.
abstract: This paper introduces a new optimization algorithm, termed Adaptive Topological Transformation-Driven Optimization (ATTO), that leverages the principles of adaptive topological transformation to dynamically adjust the structure of the search space during the optimization process. Traditional optimization methods often require manual adjustments, limiting their adaptability and effectiveness. The ATTO algorithm automates this adjustment, resulting in improved performance and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the continuous, self-adjusting transformation of the search space, guided by a feedback loop, optimizing for specific performance metrics. This adaptive approach offers a significant departure from conventional methods, promising a more robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in several benchmark datasets. The analysis highlights the advantages of the adaptive topology approach compared to existing optimization techniques. The resulting algorithm offers a promising advancement in the field of optimization, particularly for complex and dynamic problem domains.

title: Adaptive Polymorphic Programming
abstract: Adaptive Polymorphic Programming (APP) presents a novel approach to software development centered around dynamic adaptation of programming paradigms. The core concept involves a runtime system that leverages machine learning to determine the most suitable programming paradigm – imperative, functional, or object-oriented – for a given computational task. This system then performs automatic code translation, creating a dynamic code generation layer. Unlike traditional compiler optimizations, APP offers a fundamentally adaptive environment, aiming to maximize both performance and code clarity. This paper details the architecture, key components, and theoretical underpinnings of the APP system, highlighting its potential to revolutionize software development by enabling truly context-aware and optimized code execution. The system's efficacy is predicated on a predictive machine learning model trained on a diverse set of programming tasks and their corresponding execution profiles. The system's output is a dynamically translated code representation, represented mathematically as: *C' = f(C, T, M)* Where: * *C* represents the original input code. * *C'* represents the dynamically translated code. * *T* represents the current computational task (defined by its inputs and constraints). * *M* represents the machine learning model's prediction of the optimal programming paradigm. * *f* represents the translation function which maps *C*, *T*, and *M* to *C'*. This framework allows for a continuous feedback loop, allowing the machine learning model to refine its predictions over time. The system's performance is evaluated based on metrics such as execution time, memory usage, and code complexity, with the objective of minimizing the latter while maximizing the former. Further investigation into the scalability and generalizability of the APP system is warranted. ---

title: Density Peak Representative Point Data Stream Clustering for Radar Signal Sorting
abstract: Radar signal sorting based on data stream clustering has attracted increasing attention in complex electromagnetic environments.However, existing methods often suffer from limited capability in representing complex cluster structures and difficulty in continuously tracking the evolutionary behavior of radar emitters.To address these issues, this paper proposes a radar signal sorting method based on density-peak representative points within a data stream clustering framework.The proposed method adopts an initialization-online update architecture.In the initialization stage, the I-OPTICS algorithm is employed to obtain the initial cluster structure, and the representative point radius is adaptively determined using the inflection point of the k-nearest neighbor distance curve.Representative points are then generated based on the density peak strategy to construct micro-clusters.In the online stage, fast data assignment is achieved through representative point coverage, while emitter evolution behaviors are detected using a time-decay mechanism and an outlier buffer strategy.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves detection rate of 91.59% and processing speed of 28,735 pulses/s on the simulated PDW dataset, outperforming several baseline algorithms in both sorting accuracy and computational efficiency.In addition, the proposed method can effectively track the evolutionary behaviors of radar emitters in dynamic data stream environments.

title: Credit Card Fraud Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance: A Comparison of KNN and Logistic Regression
abstract: Credit card fraud is a serious threat in the digital financial ecosystem and is characterised by extreme class imbalance, with fraudulent transactions typically below 1%. This study compares two standard classification algorithms, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and Logistic Regression (LR), for detecting fraudulent transactions on the Sparkov dataset (1.85 million transactions; a stratified subsample of 100,000 rows; 0.52% fraud rate), and analyses the effect of the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Preprocessing includes temporal feature engineering, haversine distance, leak-free per-card behavioural features, one-hot and label encoding, and z-score standardisation. Models are evaluated on a stratified 80:20 split using the confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC, complemented by decision-threshold tuning, confidence intervals over five repetitions, and the McNemar test. No single model dominates across all metrics. At the default threshold, KNN baseline achieves the highest F1 (0.407) and precision (0.540), while LR baseline achieves the highest PR-AUC (0.246); LR+SMOTE leads on recall (0.712) and ROC-AUC (0.861) but with very low precision (0.025). Threshold tuning lets LR baseline reach the best F1 (0.422 at a 0.071 cut-off). McNemar shows the KNN–LR difference is not significant at baseline (p = 0.282) but significant under SMOTE (p < 0.001). The main finding is that under severe imbalance ROC-AUC can be misleading and PR-AUC is more informative; KNN baseline is a balanced detector without tuning, threshold-tuned LR baseline gives the best single operating point, and LR+SMOTE suits cases where recall is the priority.

title: SISTEM PAKAR SKRINING GEJALA DISMENORE DAN PEMBOBOTAN AWAL MENGGUNAKAN METODE FORWARD CHAINING
abstract: Dysmenorrhea, or menstrual pain, is the most common gynecological issue experienced by women of childbearing age, particularly adolescent girls. Although it is a natural physiological process, high-intensity pain can significantly disrupt comfort and temporarily paralyze daily productivity. Many women tend to ignore these symptoms due to a lack of information regarding the long-term impacts on reproductive health, as well as time and cost constraints for direct medical consultations. Therefore, this study aims to design and implement a web-based expert system as an instrument for the early detection (screening) of dysmenorrhea symptoms. This expert system adopts a medical knowledge base to classify dysmenorrhea into two categories: primary dysmenorrhea and secondary dysmenorrhea. The reasoning logic applied in this system utilizes an inference engine with the Forward Chaining method, which operates on a data-driven reasoning approach. This method initiates tracking from a set of facts or symptoms inputted by the user to derive a final diagnostic conclusion. To enhance screening accuracy, the system integrates an initial weighting technique on the symptom variables, considering that each clinical sign possesses a different level of significance. The system is built using the Python programming language with the Streamlit framework, featuring an interactive and user-friendly interface. The output generated by the expert system consists of a conclusion on the dysmenorrhea category, visualized certainty percentages, and measured initial management recommendations. Through this independent platform, it is expected that women can screen their reproductive health conditions quickly, accurately, and objectively, thereby minimizing the risk of further complications at an early stage.

title: Good Memory Has ECC: Evaluating the Memory of Vision-Language Models Beyond Accuracy
abstract: Memory is widely viewed as an important unsolved problem for LLMs and VLMs, and current benchmarks typically evaluate it by testing accuracy over long text or video. However, accuracy alone misses properties that matter for real long-horizon tasks. We introduce ECCBench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that measures memory beyond a system's capacity--its raw accuracy at a specific budget--via three axes we call ECC: efficiency--the computation, in FLOPs, needed to answer from memory; compression--whether compressible inputs are remembered more accurately or efficiently; and calibration--whether the system abstains in response to its own uncertainty and the cost of an error. We find that pretrained VLMs compress their memory over text but not video and are poorly calibrated on both. Among a broader set of memory backbones, several non-Transformer architectures achieve better compression-calibration tradeoffs than RoPE Transformers, suggesting they may be useful components for agents operating over long horizons.

title: Exponential random graph models with soft clique constraints
abstract: Let $r\geq3$ be fixed, and let $\mathbf{G}_n$ be the set of all simple graphs with vertex set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. We consider an exponential random graph model which gives higher probability to $G \in \mathbf{G}_n$ than to $H \in \mathbf{G}_n$ if $G$ has fewer $r$-cliques than $H$. But all graphs in $\mathbf{G}_n$ have positive probability. The degree to which graphs with fewer $r$-cliques are given higher probability is determined by a positive weight $w$. We prove that, asymptotically almost surely as $n \to \infty$, a random graph from $\mathbf{G}_n$ has a vertex partition into $r-1$ parts of roughly equal size, the density of edges between the parts is close to $1/2$, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the density of edges within any part is less than $\varepsilon$. The asymptotic structural properties are independent of the weight $w$ as long as it is positive. We also extend the result to the context of several clique sizes, each one with its own weight.

title: SemPOI-RL: Aligning LLM Semantic Reasoning for Interpretable Out-of-Town POI Sequential Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong semantic reasoning and open-ended generation abilities, but aligning these abilities with structured sequential generation remains challenging. This challenge is particularly evident in out-of-town (OOT) POI sequence generation, where a model must infer transferable travel intent from a user's hometown behaviors, adapt to cross-city interest drift, and generate a coherent destination trajectory under structural constraints. Existing approaches either rely on latent ID-based transfer with limited interpretability or directly use LLMs for sequence generation without explicitly grounding inferred semantics into position-aware predictions. To address this gap, we propose SemPOI-RL, a framework that aligns LLM semantic reasoning with structured sequence generation for interpretable OOT recommendation. Specifically, we first fine-tune an LLM to infer destination-oriented travel styles from users' hometown trajectories, using natural language as an interpretable semantic intermediate. We then introduce a Semantic POI Alignment Module (SPAM) to ground these inferred styles into a style-conditioned masked autoencoder for position-aware trajectory generation. Finally, we apply reinforcement learning with recommendation-oriented rewards to align LLM-generated styles with downstream sequence quality. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that SemPOI-RL consistently outperforms both traditional recommenders and direct LLM baselines, while providing interpretable style attribution across different phases of a trip. The code is available at https://github.com/Wind-Flipped/SemPOI-RL .

title: Adaptiiviset variaatioalgoritmit kvanttikemian simulaatioissa
abstract: Quantum computers offer a promising solution to the challenges posed by the exponentially increasing computational demands of quantum chemistry simulations. However, due to the noise, decoherence, and error rates of current NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) devices, deep quantum circuits are unsuitable for large-scale simulations, as they lead to accumulating errors and optimization difficulties. The objective of this thesis is to present the theoretical background of quantum chemistry simulations and to evaluate the performance of the dynamic ADAPT-VQE (Adaptive Derivative-Assembled Problem-Tailored Variational Quantum Eigensolver) algorithm in molecular simulations. The theoretical section covers the fundamentals of quantum computing, the modeling of the physical quantum-mechanical properties of molecules on quantum computers, and the advantages offered by the ADAPT-VQE algorithm in simulations. In the practical section, the operation of the ADAPT-VQE algorithm was investigated by simulating the potential energy surface of a hydrogen molecule, determining the molecule’s ground state, and visualizing the electron density distribution in spatial coordinates. The simulation was implemented in a noise-free state vector environment using Python. The results of the simulation demonstrated that the ADAPT-VQE algorithm identifies the ground state energy of the hydrogen molecule accurately and rapidly. In calculating the total energy of the molecule, the algorithm achieved the required standard of chemical accuracy and an absolute error of only 0.1 nanohartree after just a single iteration. The spatial distribution of the hydrogen molecule’s electron density was also modeled based on the quantum state determined by the algorithm. The distribution displayed a correlation with the molecule’s covalent bond. This thesis confirms that the ADAPT-VQE algorithm is capable of reducing quantum circuit depth by adding only the most physically significant operators. This hardware-efficient feature is critical when scaling simulations to larger molecules on noisy quantum computers.

title: Exploration of AIGC-Enabled Teaching Model for “Big Data Platform Construction and Maintenance” Course in Higher Vocational Education
abstract: In response to the challenges of disconnection between theory and practice, outdated resources, and significant variations in student proficiency in the traditional teaching of Big Data Platform Construction and Maintenance courses in higher vocational education, this paper proposes an AIGC-enabled course teaching model from the perspective of constructivist learning theory. The model deeply integrates AIGC tools into the entire process of “pre-class preparation, in-class guidance, and post-class consolidation,” constructing four key dimensions: professional resource generation, personalized learning diagnosis, situated practice support, and iterative professional capability development. Through practical application in actual teaching, results demonstrate that this model effectively enhances students’ troubleshooting and cluster maintenance capabilities, with students’ final comprehensive scores and willingness for independent learning significantly improved compared to the traditional model. This research provides a practical reference for the human-machine collaborative teaching reform of big data courses in higher vocational education.

title: РОЗДІЛ 7. МЕТОД АДАПТИВНОГО ВИБОРУ ПОЧАТКОВИХ СТАНІВ ДЛЯ НАВЧАННЯ DQN-АГЕНТА В СЕРЕДОВИЩАХ ІЗ РІЗНИМИ ТИПАМИ ҐРУНТІВ
abstract: РОЗДІЛ 7 МЕТОД АДАПТИВНОГО ВИБОРУ ПОЧАТКОВИХ СТАНІВ ДЛЯ НАВЧАННЯ DQN-АГЕНТА В СЕРЕДОВИЩАХ ІЗ РІЗНИМИ ТИПАМИ ҐРУНТІВ Драган Михайло Сергійович, аспірант кафедри ІСТ, ФІОТ, Національний технічний університет України «Київський політехнічний інститут імені Ігоря Сікорського», Київ, Україна Навчання автономних транспортних засобів із підкріпленням потребує формування політики, здатної працювати за межами умов, представлених під час навчання.Фіксовані початкові стани спрощують пошук стратегії, однак підвищують ризик перенавчання та запам'ятовування окремих траєкторій.У попередній роботі авторів показано, що зміна початкових позицій поліпшує узагальнення DQN-агента на складній гоночній трасі.Випадковий вибір початкових станів не враховує складності окремих ділянок і може створювати незбалансований навчальний набір.Ця проблема стає суттєвішою в середовищах із різними типами ґрунтів, де довжина маршруту не завжди відповідає складності його проходження.Для оцінювання початкових станів доцільно враховувати зважену вартість руху, яка залежить від властивостей місцевості.Метою роботи є підвищення швидкості та стабільності навчання DQNагента шляхом адаптивного вибору початкових станів.Запропонований метод використовує планувальник руху для розподілу початкових станів за складністю та змінює ймовірність їх вибору відповідно до поточної успішності агента.Експеримент передбачає порівняння фіксованого, рівномірного випадкового, збалансованого й адаптивного способів формування початкових умов, а також дослідження впливу частоти їх зміни.Глибоке Q-навчання поєднує навчання з підкріпленням із нейронною апроксимацією функції цінності дій.Застосування буфера досвіду та окремої

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Historical Development Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. title: Title: Cognitive Mapping & Simulated Neural Networks
abstract: Cognitive Mapping & Simulated Neural Networks explores the integration of cognitive maps into simulated neural network training, aiming to foster the creation of increasingly sophisticated AI agents. The core mechanism centers around creating a system where an agent's understanding of its environment is explicitly represented as a cognitive map, which is then leveraged to guide the training of a simulated neural network. This approach addresses limitations of current methods, which often prioritize raw data without grounding the learning process in a meaningful, holistic representation of the agent's knowledge. The research investigates how such a framework enhances agent learning through a combination of representation learning and reinforcement-based optimization. This paper presents a novel methodology for training and evaluating such a system, detailing the design of a cognitive map and a corresponding simulated neural network architecture. The paper concludes by discussing the potential implications of this integration for advancing AI agent capabilities and reasoning.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Exploration Bonuses
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework designed to address the challenges of exploration in high-dimensional state spaces, a persistent issue within standard reinforcement learning paradigms. The core idea centers around integrating intrinsic motivation, specifically curiosity and surprise, alongside dynamically adjusted exploration bonuses. We hypothesize that this combined approach will significantly enhance the agent's ability to discover rewarding states effectively. The proposed architecture utilizes a hierarchical structure, allowing for strategic decomposition of complex tasks into simpler, more manageable sub-goals. The intrinsic motivation component encourages the agent to actively seek out novel and unexpected states, while the exploration bonuses provide a mechanism for further refinement of this behavior. Through this combination, we aim to create an HRL system that is both more efficient and robust in its exploration strategy, leading to faster learning and improved performance in challenging environments. The key contributions lie in the synergistic interaction between hierarchical decision-making, intrinsic drive, and adaptive exploration. We will demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, focusing on scenarios where traditional exploration methods fall short.

title: 基于生物几何的量子计算模拟
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing simulation framework predicated on the principles of biological geometry. Traditional quantum computing simulations often struggle with the complexities inherent in biological systems, necessitating specialized models and often limited computational capabilities. We propose a new approach that integrates biological geometry, specifically the hierarchical structure of biological forms, into the core of our quantum algorithms. This integration aims to enhance the precision and efficiency of quantum simulations, particularly in modeling systems with intricate geometries and dynamic behaviors. The core mechanism centers on embedding geometric constraints and relationships into the quantum circuit design, leveraging the inherent properties of biological forms to guide computational processes. The research explores the potential for this integration to unlock new avenues for simulating biological data and advancing our understanding of complex biological phenomena.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Resolution
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm designed for enhanced constraint resolution, aiming to significantly accelerate and improve the accuracy of solving constraint satisfaction problems. Traditional constraint resolution methods often struggle with large, complex constraint sets, limiting their applicability in areas like software development, optimization, and artificial intelligence. We introduce a quantum-enhanced approach that utilizes superposition and entanglement to explore the solution space more efficiently, potentially unlocking solutions previously intractable with classical algorithms. The core mechanism focuses on a quantum search algorithm tailored for constraint set manipulation, demonstrating promising results through simulations and preliminary analysis. The potential impact of this research is considerable, offering a pathway towards more robust and scalable constraint resolution techniques.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design, termed Dynamic Neuron Topology Adaptive Learning (DNTAL). The core claim of this method is that the connection strength and topology of neurons can dynamically adapt to task requirements, thereby improving learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. This is achieved through a mechanism combining genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning. The system continuously evaluates the effectiveness of the neuron topology and adjusts both connection strengths and topology based on the evaluation results. Unlike traditional neural networks with fixed topologies, DNTAL provides the network with the ability to self-evolve and adapt, mirroring the self-organizing characteristics of biological neural systems. The proposed framework addresses a key limitation of conventional neural networks – the lack of adaptability – offering a potential pathway to more efficient and robust learning systems. The evaluation focuses on demonstrating the improved performance of DNTAL compared to fixed topology networks in a simulated environment.

title: Non-Linear Geometry Topology and Quantum Computing: A Synergistic Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the potential synergistic relationship between non-linear geometry topology and quantum computation. We explore the design of a novel quantum computing framework that leverages the inherent robustness and structural properties of non-linear geometry to enhance quantum computation's resilience to noise and improve algorithmic efficiency. The core claim is that incorporating a quantum-based structure, inspired by topological properties, can significantly increase the robustness and performance of quantum algorithms. This work presents a conceptual framework and initial design considerations for such a system, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in both areas. The paper will begin with a review of the foundational concepts of quantum geometry and its connection to topological quantum computation. It then outlines the proposed framework, detailing the role of quantum bits within this system and the mechanisms by which the topological structure enhances quantum processing. Finally, this paper will discuss future research directions and potential applications of this integrated approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Parallel Computing
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the use of quantum entanglement to drive parallel computation, specifically targeting tasks requiring intricate information transfer and intricate calculations. We investigate novel parallel computing models predicated on the manipulation of entangled states to achieve significant performance improvements. The core claim posits that leveraging quantum entanglement offers a pathway to transcend the limitations of classical parallel processing, facilitating complex calculations with enhanced efficiency. We argue that the unique properties of entanglement can fundamentally alter the way computations are performed, leading to a new era of parallel computing.

title: Building a Multimodal Emotion-Infused Distributed Knowledge Graph
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to constructing a distributed knowledge graph enriched with multimodal emotional information. Current knowledge graphs predominantly rely on textual data, limiting their ability to capture the nuanced and dynamic nature of human understanding. We introduce a framework for integrating textual, acoustic, and visual emotional cues—specifically, sentiment from text (s), emotional tone from speech (t), and facial expressions (f)—into a comprehensive knowledge graph. The core claim is that incorporating these diverse emotional signals significantly enhances the completeness and dynamism of knowledge representation, revealing the crucial role of emotion in knowledge acquisition and inference. This work leverages advancements in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Speech Recognition, and Image Recognition to extract emotional features, which are then linked to entities and relationships within the graph. We define the knowledge graph structure as G = (V, E), where V represents the set of entities and relationships, and E represents the set of connections between them. The emotional features associated with each entity and relation are represented as vectors: si, ti, and fi. The relationships between entities are described by the following formula: Rij = F(si, ti, fi, vij), where Rij is the relationship between entities i and j, vij is the vector representation of the relationship, and F is the function that combines the emotional features and the relationship vector. The ultimate goal is to create a more robust and insightful knowledge representation capable of capturing the complexities of human cognition and interaction.

title: ## Black-flanked Wallaby: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black-flanked Wallaby (BFW), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Macropus falconis*, commonly known as the black-flanked wallaby. Observing their efficient and adaptive search strategies in natural environments, we have developed a new algorithm designed for complex optimization problems. BFW mimics the wallaby's movement pattern, utilizing a concept of "tracking" and "scanning" to explore the search space. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where individuals represent potential solutions. A key element of BFW is the 'black flank' mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the probability of movement based on the perceived desirability of the surrounding environment, mimicking the wallaby's selective attention to promising areas. The algorithm's parameters, including the scanning range and flank adjustment rate, are carefully tuned to balance exploration and exploitation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BFW through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's design is inherently robust and adaptable, and its core principles offer potential for application in a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Replication code for the leakage-premium study
abstract: leakcheck screens reported binary classification summaries for a controlled resampling-before-splitting signature. Version v1.0.1 uses a screening score and neutral review bands, rejects unsupported model families with ValueError, and keeps the existing v1.0.0 JSON model unchanged (SHA-256 6ad86351f6458c2318e7e88426dd67f3262b94d020753d245ef600df6ff25aa1). The controlled corpus has 11,200 matched comparisons from 41 source datasets. Dataset-held-out AUC is 0.795 (cluster interval 0.743–0.849). Baselines, grouped uncertainty, per-source results, input sensitivity, and JSON-only interface demonstrations accompany the code. The full model has not demonstrated an advantage over F1-only or logistic baselines. The score is not a probability that a paper contains leakage. External diagnostic validation, hosted CI and a numerical test-coverage percentage have not been established.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum-adaptive optimization algorithm designed to address challenges in computationally intensive optimization tasks. The core concept revolves around employing quantum mechanics to simulate the optimization process, allowing for a fundamentally different approach compared to conventional optimization methods. We introduce a quantum-driven simulation framework that utilizes quantum properties to accelerate the algorithm's execution and potentially discover novel solutions. This work explores the potential of quantum computing to improve the performance of optimization problems across various domains, offering a promising alternative for scenarios where classical methods struggle. The research focuses on a specific, yet impactful, application: optimizing a complex, multi-dimensional function with intricate constraints. The algorithm's design incorporates key elements such as quantum state manipulation and entanglement to achieve improved convergence and solution quality. This paper details the theoretical underpinnings, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness. We will also discuss the challenges and future directions for this research, including exploring the scalability of the quantum-adaptive approach.

title: Hierarchical Memory Networks with Adaptive Contextual Abstraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hierarchical memory network architecture designed to overcome the limitations of traditional memory networks concerning long-term dependencies and scalability. The core of the proposed approach lies in incorporating adaptive contextual abstraction layers, which enable the network to dynamically adjust the granularity of information storage and processing. Lower levels are dedicated to retaining fine-grained details, while higher levels perform abstraction and summarization, creating a hierarchical structure that significantly improves the network's ability to capture and utilize complex, long-range relationships within data. The architecture is designed to address the challenges of managing vast contextual information, leading to enhanced performance in tasks requiring memory of extended sequences. The key innovation is the dynamic adjustment of abstraction levels, achieved through a learned mechanism, allowing the network to efficiently process information at varying levels of detail. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a potential implementation strategy.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Distribution
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a cornerstone of quantum computing and quantum communication, promising transformative capabilities. However, maintaining entanglement over significant distances presents a significant hurdle due to decoherence. This paper explores a novel adaptive system for distributing quantum entanglement, designed to dynamically adjust entanglement strength based on observation. We propose a feedback loop that continuously monitors the entanglement strength and optimizes distribution to preserve coherence. The core mechanism centers around a continuous assessment and adjustment of entanglement parameters, addressing a critical challenge in long-distance quantum information processing. This work offers a promising approach to enhancing entanglement distribution and mitigating decoherence effects.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction and Decentralized Execution
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) that leverages hierarchical temporal abstraction (HTA) and decentralized execution for enhanced coordination and learning efficiency. Traditional MARL methods often struggle with scalability issues, particularly in environments with a large number of agents and complex interactions. Our proposed system addresses this challenge by introducing a hierarchical structure where agents operate at different temporal abstraction scales, facilitating efficient communication and coordination without centralized control. We utilize HTA to decompose complex tasks into simpler, more manageable sub-tasks, reducing the state space and improving learning speed. The decentralized execution allows each agent to learn and act independently based on its local observations and the abstracted goals provided by its higher-level controller. The core claim of this work is to design a multi-agent RL system that utilizes hierarchical temporal abstraction and decentralized execution for efficient coordination and learning in complex environments. This research provides a robust and scalable framework for tackling challenging MARL problems.
