title: Quantum-Resilient Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Review of Ethical Governance and Regulatory Frameworks
abstract: Quantum computing poses a severe threat to standard digital security protocols, leaving artificial intelligence (AI) data pipelines and decision-support systems highly exposed. As large-scale quantum attacks become computationally feasible, the public-key cryptography currently securing data transmission will likely fail. This vulnerability threatens sectors heavily reliant on AI—including finance, healthcare, and critical infrastructure escalating the probability of data breaches, integrity losses, and compliance failures. To address these interconnected security, governance, and ethical hurdles, this paper introduces the Integrated Quantum-Resilient AI Framework (IQRAI). IQRAI establishes a structured governance model combining proactive quantum risk assessments, post-quantum cryptography (PQC), and continuous security monitoring. A core focus of the framework is balancing cryptographic migration with strict ethical requirements, specifically data privacy, algorithmic transparency, fairness, and auditability. Furthermore, the study reviews ongoing global standardization efforts for PQC transitions to define baseline requirements for sustained system resilience. By comparing existing mitigation models across metrics of operational friction, implementation difficulty, and security yield, the research identifies a critical operational gap. The analysis demonstrates that merely swapping cryptographic algorithms is insufficient for achieving quantum-resilient AI; securing these systems demands a unified approach that links security engineering, ethical oversight, and regulatory adherence. Ultimately, this work delivers a strategic roadmap for organizations to systematically harden their AI ecosystems against quantum threats while maintaining operational trust and legal compliance.

title: From Drift Detection to Diagnosis: An Explainable Framework for Deployed Machine Learning
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models are increasingly deployed in real-world environments where data characteristics, user behaviour, and operating conditions may change over time. Such changes can lead to data or concept drift and may gradually reduce model reliability. Existing monitoring approaches can identify distributional changes or performance degradation, but they often provide limited information about why the changes occur. Similarly, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods can explain model predictions but are frequently treated separately from continuous drift monitoring. This paper proposes a unified drift-aware framework for explainable diagnostics in deployed machine learning systems. The framework integrates data-drift detection, model-performance monitoring, explainability, and diagnostic decision-making into a continuous monitoring pipeline. Statistical drift detection methods are used to identify changes between reference and production data, while XAI techniques such as SHAP and LIME are used to identify important features associated with changes in model behaviour. The framework combines drift indicators and performance information to generate interpretable diagnostic reports and recommend suitable maintenance actions. The proposed approach aims to improve the transparency, reliability, and maintainability of deployed ML systems by connecting drift detection with actionable explanations. The framework can support proactive model monitoring and assist practitioners in deciding whether continued monitoring, investigation, recalibration, or model retraining is required. Keywords: Explainable AI,Machine Learning Deployment, Model Monitoring,Drift Detection

The proposed approach aims to improve the transparency, reliability, and maintainability of deployed ML systems by connecting drift detection with actionable explanations. title: SCILLA v1.1.0 Synthetic Evidence
abstract: This dataset is the reproducibility and robustness evidence companion to the SCILLA v1.1.0 canonical research note (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22209746). It contains the synthetic evidence used to audit and reproduce the principal computational results of SCILLA, including matched run-level results, aggregate policy effects, paired-bootstrap confidence intervals, sign-flip tests, parameter sensitivity sweeps, prior-mismatch and other ablation experiments, independent trace-verifier results, canonical trace records, the frozen experimental protocol, assumptions, and seed registry. The evidence preserves both positive and negative results. In particular, the released experiments do not support universal adaptive superiority for raw discovery. The dataset instead supports more bounded findings concerning paired ascent/return reacquisition, the constructed priority-weighted Track Debt metric, and decision-weighted utility under the declared synthetic reference conditions. All performance data contained in this record are synthetic or recomputed from the released SCILLA research software. No physical SCILLA field measurement is included. The dataset does not establish operational detection range, field tracking performance, customer ROI, patent status, QPU execution, or quantum advantage. An independent trace verifier is included in the associated evidence architecture to recompute geometry, eligibility, scan constraints, observation identities, paired-state counts, and final metric identities without selecting the optimizer’s actions. This dataset supplements the canonical SCILLA v1.1.0 research publication: Michele Giletto, “SCILLA: Altitude-Coupled Transient Maritime Surface Observation — Geometry, Paired State Estimation, and Falsification of Adaptive Scan Allocation,” Giletto Systems Lab, v1.1.0, 2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22209746. The next validation gates are external historical sensor replay and a cooperative paired-observation field experiment using synchronized platform navigation and independent target ground truth.

title: Effects-and-Lifetimes Calculus — Mechanized Safety Proofs
abstract: A Rocq (Coq) formalization of a call-by-value calculus with bounded type polymorphism (full F<:), a separate lifetime sort forming a two-point lattice, algebraic data constructors with existential lifetime/type schemas, and algebraic effect handlers with multi-shot resumptions — the proof-side companion of the CoreΔ calculus. The safety story is lifetime-based capability confinement: effect capabilities are local-annotated values, and the lifetime subtyping discipline guarantees that neither a capability nor any local-confined datum can escape the scope that delimits it. The development is axiom-free — every capstone theorem prints «Closed under the global context» under Print Assumptions, enforced by a derived assumption gate (make verify). It includes type soundness, capability confinement at every syntactic occurrence, guarded handler-boundary theorems on states and on labelled transition events with a certified completeness accounting, determinism modulo the fresh-marker choice, certified reflected deciders and a certified evaluator with an OCaml extraction, and a fully verified examples tier with a rejection suite. See README.md for the theorem table and ARTIFACT.md for the build and verification guide.

title: Dynamic Topology for Machine Learning Model Evaluation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for evaluating machine learning models based on dynamic topology. Traditional evaluation methods often rely on manual design, limiting the model's adaptability. Our proposed system automatically adjusts the model's topology based on training data and model performance, enhancing generalization capabilities. We present a dynamic topology construction algorithm that iteratively refines the model's representation, leading to improved robustness and performance across diverse datasets. The framework's core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent properties of dynamic topology to dynamically shape the model's representation, fostering better generalization. This approach significantly reduces the need for extensive manual tuning and allows for more effective model optimization.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of topological quantum entanglement, a paradigm shift from traditional qubit-based systems, by exploring a novel 'folding' process to generate and manipulate persistent entanglement patterns. We propose a method that dynamically shapes the topology of a quantum system, creating persistent entanglement without the need for explicit qubit manipulation. This approach offers a fundamentally new pathway to robust and scalable entanglement, potentially unlocking applications in quantum computing and communication. The core claim is to develop a robust method for generating and manipulating topological quantum states, extending entanglement beyond traditional qubit-based systems. This research utilizes a dynamically shaped 'folding' process to establish persistent entanglement without requiring traditional qubit manipulation. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced stability and adaptability, offering a significant advancement in the field of topological quantum entanglement.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential to revolutionize information encoding and transmission. title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Grammars and Neural Network Guidance
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a technique that aims to automatically discover mathematical expressions from data. Despite its potential, SR often struggles to find complex and interpretable models due to the vast number of possible solutions that need to be explored. This work proposes a novel approach that combines evolutionary grammars with neural network guidance to improve the efficiency and robustness of SR. The core idea is to use an evolutionary grammar system to generate a diverse range of symbolic expressions and then leverage a neural network to prioritize expressions with higher predicted fitness. The neural network is trained to predict the fitness of expressions based on their characteristics, allowing the evolutionary algorithm to focus on more promising candidates. This integrated framework demonstrates improved performance in discovering complex mathematical models compared to traditional SR methods, offering a more effective strategy for tackling challenging SR problems. The key equations and concepts explored in this paper are: * Error Metric: E = Σ |yi - f(xi)| * Fitness Function: F(expression) = 1 / E * Grammar Rules: G = {R1, R2, ..., Rn} * Neural Network Output: y = NN(expression) * Evolutionary Algorithm Step: Selection → Mutation → Crossover → Replacement

title: Constraint-Driven Quantum State Collapse
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, Constraint-Driven Quantum State Collapse, designed to enhance the fidelity of quantum measurements through dynamic constraint feedback. The core mechanism centers on continuous monitoring of the quantum state and adaptive adjustment of constraints to induce a specific collapse trajectory. This approach aims to overcome limitations inherent in traditional quantum measurement techniques by offering a mechanism to directly influence the collapse process. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy in improving measurement fidelity. The paper concludes by highlighting the potential for this approach to advance the state of quantum measurement accuracy.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Style Transfer for Enhanced Generalization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, offering the potential for more robust and adaptable models. A key challenge in QML lies in the inherent difficulty of training models on data with varying styles or characteristics. This paper proposes a novel approach to address this challenge – Style Transfer, specifically tailored for QML. We investigate a method leveraging stylistic features extracted from data, effectively migrating these features to improve the model's generalization across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves carefully extracting and adapting stylistic elements, promoting better representation learning and improved robustness. This research explores the potential of stylistic transfer to enhance the performance of QML models, ultimately offering a pathway to more versatile and reliable AI systems.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Distributed Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed verification leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed verification systems often rely on computationally intensive cryptographic algorithms, which are vulnerable to attacks and may introduce latency. This research introduces a system that utilizes entangled states to provide a trustless, real-time verification of computations across distributed nodes. The core mechanism involves establishing an entangled state between nodes, continuously monitoring the computation process, and detecting any attempts at data manipulation or node impersonation by observing changes in the entangled state. The proposed system offers a fundamentally different security paradigm, capitalizing on the inherent properties of quantum mechanics for enhanced security potential compared to conventional cryptographic methods. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the key equations and mathematical relationships involved in the entanglement-based verification process. The system's performance characteristics and security guarantees are discussed. ---

title: Biofeedback Control of Artificial Neuron Model Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to optimizing artificial neuron models by leveraging biofeedback signals. The core concept involves establishing a closed-loop feedback system where the output of an artificial neuron directly influences the adjustment of its internal parameters. This process utilizes optimization algorithms, such as genetic algorithms or particle swarm optimization, driven by the biofeedback signal, aiming to achieve more realistic neural computations and improved learning capabilities. Unlike conventional methods reliant on manually designed activation functions and connection weights, this biofeedback control offers an adaptive and potentially more efficient optimization strategy. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, presents a mathematical model, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges of this emerging technique. The primary focus is on the algorithmic design and control mechanisms necessary to effectively translate biofeedback data into parameter adjustments within the artificial neuron model. Further research will explore the scalability and applicability of this approach across diverse neural network architectures and biofeedback modalities.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Information Analysis Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked regardless of distance, has emerged as a promising resource for advanced information processing and quantum technologies. This research explores the application of quantum entanglement to the analysis of topological information, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of topological information analysis. We propose an algorithm that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to represent and manipulate topological data, offering a novel approach to address limitations inherent in classical methods. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the entanglement to capture the dynamic nature of topological structures, ultimately leading to a more precise understanding of these intricate phenomena. The algorithm utilizes a modified version of the entanglement-induced measurement protocol, where entangled states are manipulated to reveal subtle topological features. This represents a significant step towards a more robust and accurate method for analyzing topological data, potentially unlocking new insights into the underlying physics of these systems. The significance of this work lies in the potential for quantum entanglement to provide a fundamentally different perspective on topological information analysis, offering a pathway to overcoming classical computational constraints and advancing the field.

title: ## Beach Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Sand Hopper," inspired by the foraging behavior of beach voles. Beach voles are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies when seeking food resources on beaches. This algorithm leverages their movement patterns, incorporating elements of randomness, local optimization, and adaptive exploration to address complex optimization problems. The core of Sand Hopper revolves around a "sand hopper" representation, where each solution is modeled as a sand particle moving within a simulated beach environment. The algorithm employs a modified version of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) concept, with a novel beach terrain generation mechanism to promote exploration and exploitation. We detail the algorithm's mechanics, including the generation of the beach terrain, the movement of sand hoppers, and the adaptation of individual hopper parameters. The performance of Sand Hopper is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic approaches. The key contributions of this work include a novel algorithm design, a comprehensive analysis of its parameters, and a comparative evaluation against established optimization methods. The results indicate that Sand Hopper offers a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization scenarios.

title: Quantum Delay Compensation Mechanism in Quantum Networks
abstract: Quantum networks promise secure and efficient communication, but significant delays introduce critical limitations for long-distance quantum key distribution (QKD) and other quantum network applications. This paper presents a novel mechanism for precise delay compensation within quantum networks, leveraging quantum entanglement and interference. The core idea involves real-time measurement and correction of time delays using entangled photon pairs. We formally define the problem, propose a compensation strategy based on a feedback loop utilizing Bell state measurements and subsequent phase adjustments. The theoretical framework outlines the mathematical models and key equations governing the system, including those describing entanglement evolution, time delay propagation, and the measurement process. We explore the impact of various delay characteristics on the effectiveness of the compensation and discuss potential improvements and scaling challenges. The results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential to significantly enhance the robustness and range of quantum networks.

Traditional approaches often fail to fully exploit the inherent properties of entangled states, leading to complex protocols and vulnerabilities. We detail the mechanism through which the model achieves this, emphasizing the importance of utilizing the self-similarity inherent in topological concepts to simplify quantum operations. This work offers a potentially transformative approach to quantum information processing, addressing limitations of current quantum algorithms and communication protocols.

title: Balsas Mouse Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Unique Physiological Adaptations of a Neotenic Mammal
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Balsas Mouse Opossum" (BMO), inspired by the remarkable physiological adaptations of the Balsas mouse opossum (*Marmosops balsae*). This neotenic mammal exhibits a unique combination of embryonic retention, delayed maturation, and facultative hibernation, allowing it to thrive in a challenging, fluctuating environment. BMO leverages these biological principles to develop an algorithm designed for complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates elements of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and a novel 'dormancy' mechanism based on the opossum's hibernation cycle. Specifically, BMO utilizes a population of potential solutions, each with an initial temperature (representing metabolic activity) and a dormancy level. The temperature decreases over time, simulating seasonal changes and energy conservation, while the dormancy level reflects the solution's stability. The algorithm's core update mechanism involves both exploration (movement of particles) and exploitation (local refinement), guided by the temperature and dormancy level. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BMO through a series of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The results suggest that BMO is capable of finding optimal or near-optimal solutions for a range of challenging problems, demonstrating the viability of bio-inspired algorithms for complex optimization tasks.

title: 基于有限域的量子纠缠的概率推理
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging limited-domain quantum entanglement for probabilistic reasoning. Traditional approaches to quantum entanglement reasoning often rely on complex quantum computations, limiting the ability to effectively harness the inherent probabilistic nature of the phenomenon. We propose a novel framework utilizing limited-domain quantum entanglement, focusing on the probabilistic properties of entangled states. This framework offers improved efficiency and a more intuitive approach to probabilistic inference, potentially revolutionizing the way we reason about quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around encoding and manipulating entanglement states within a restricted Hilbert space, enabling probabilistic modeling and enhanced reasoning. We present a preliminary design and discuss the advantages and challenges of this approach, highlighting its potential for accelerating quantum computation and enhancing the precision of probabilistic analysis.

title: Negative Spider Optimization: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Negative Spider Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Negative Spider Optimization (NSO), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of negative spiders. These spiders, found in the Namib Desert, exhibit a remarkable ability to locate water sources by sensing humidity gradients. NSO mimics this process through a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation strategy, utilizing a 'negative' gradient concept to guide the search towards promising regions in the solution space. The algorithm employs a population of 'spiders', each represented by a position (s_i) in the search space. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the gradient direction, influenced by the relative humidity and water availability estimated by each spider. The algorithm incorporates a 'negative' gradient component to enhance the exploration capability and overcome local optima. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and explains how it leverages the principles observed in negative spider behavior to achieve effective optimization.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement information encryption protocol designed to achieve high security, unbreakability, and resilience against attack. title: ## Arctic Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Arctic Shrews
abstract: This paper presents Arctic Shrew, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of Arctic shrews. Arctic shrews are renowned for their unique ability to efficiently locate and exploit scattered food sources across a vast, unpredictable landscape. This paper details the algorithm's design, focusing on mimicking the shrews' adaptive exploration and exploitation phases, incorporating a novel 'memory' component to enhance search efficiency. The core of Arctic Shrew revolves around a population-based search, utilizing a modified particle representation that considers both position and 'memory' values. The algorithm employs a dynamically adjusted probability distribution for movement, influenced by the local food density. A key innovation is the 'Foraging Radius' parameter, reflecting the shrew's limited search range. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The results show that Arctic Shrew consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. title: Apennine Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Suncus apenninus*
abstract: This paper presents Apennine Shrew, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Suncus apenninus*, a small shrew species endemic to the Apennine Mountains of Italy. *Suncus apenninus* exhibits a remarkable foraging strategy characterized by intermittent searches and localized exploitation of promising areas. Apennine Shrew leverages these principles to develop a novel algorithm for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel "territoriality" mechanism that mimics the shrew's tendency to defend and revisit favored foraging locations. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic population of "shrews," each with a position and velocity, governed by a territory assignment scheme. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The key innovations of Apennine Shrew lie in its adaptive territory management, its efficient exploration-exploitation balance, and its potential for improved performance compared to traditional metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's parameterization is relatively simple, making it readily adaptable to diverse problem domains. Further research will focus on exploring the algorithm's applicability to real-world engineering and scientific challenges.

title: ## The Arctic Goose Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Goose Migration Patterns
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Goose Metaheuristic (AGM), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory behavior of Arctic geese. AGM leverages the geese's tendency to explore diverse routes, adapt to environmental changes, and maintain a balance between exploitation and exploration, mirroring their survival strategies. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a dynamic route selection system based on route diversity, an adaptive step-size adjustment mechanism influenced by environmental noise, and a population polarization strategy mimicking flock formation. AGM aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a wide range of optimization problems. The algorithm's core parameters and operational rules are described in detail, outlining its unique approach to navigating complex search spaces. This paper presents a theoretical framework for AGM and establishes its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic optimization landscape.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Fluid Dynamics with Adaptive Grid
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities in modeling complex systems, and fluid dynamics presents a particularly challenging area for computational advancements. This paper explores the application of quantum computing to enhance fluid dynamics simulations, focusing on the development of a novel adaptive grid algorithm. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent computational cost of simulating fluid flows with high resolution, limiting accuracy and scalability. This work introduces a dynamically adjusting grid scheme that optimizes the simulation by leveraging quantum phenomena to achieve significantly improved accuracy and reduced computational resources. The paper details the implementation of this adaptive grid algorithm, demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simulations, and discusses the potential implications for future research and applications in fluid dynamics.

title: Anderson's Mouse Opossum: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Behavioral Adaptation
abstract: This paper introduces Anderson's Mouse Opossum (AMO), a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm designed to address limitations observed in existing meta-heuristics. AMO draws inspiration from the adaptive foraging behavior of the opossum, specifically its ability to dynamically adjust movement strategies based on environmental feedback. The algorithm incorporates a multi-layered exploration-exploitation framework, utilizing a 'phantom' opossum concept to simulate intelligent decision-making and a dynamic 'terrain' representation to model the optimization landscape. AMO leverages a novel 'momentum-based obstacle avoidance' mechanism to enhance search efficiency and escape local optima. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating competitive results against established meta-heuristics like Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The core innovation lies in the integrated adaptive strategy mimicking the opossum's instinctive responses to its surroundings, leading to a robust and efficient optimization process. The key parameters of AMO, including the phantom opossum count, terrain resolution, and momentum coefficient, are discussed, and their impact on algorithm performance is analyzed.

title: Topology as a Constraint in Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology constraints as a novel training methodology for neural networks. Traditional training methods often rely on gradient descent, which can be susceptible to instability and suboptimal generalization. We propose a new approach that dynamically enforces topological constraints during the training process, aiming to improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of neural networks. The core mechanism involves introducing a constraint that guides the network towards maintaining a specific structural relationship between its layers, thereby mitigating issues arising from vanishing gradients and optimization instability. We present a preliminary investigation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach on a simplified neural network architecture, highlighting its potential for enhancing model performance.

title: Meta-Learning for Continuous Software System Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to achieve continuous evolution of software systems. Traditional software evolution methods often struggle to adapt to changing environments and user demands, leading to inefficiencies and potential obsolescence. We propose a novel approach that frames software system evolution as a meta-learning problem. This allows us to learn how to learn, effectively optimizing the evolutionary process itself. The core idea is to leverage meta-learning algorithms to iteratively improve the strategies used for system evolution. This results in a system that not only adapts to new requirements but also learns to adapt more effectively over time. We present a theoretical framework and outline a methodology for implementing this approach, emphasizing its potential to enhance software system adaptability and intelligence. The research contributes to a shift towards more dynamic and responsive software development practices.

title: Quantum-Based Probability Density Estimation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing for probability density estimation (PDE), a crucial component of many machine learning algorithms. Traditional PDE methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, leading to computational bottlenecks and potentially inaccurate estimates. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum circuits to perform PDE, capitalizing on quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to accelerate and potentially enhance the estimation process. Specifically, we outline a quantum algorithm designed to approximate probability density functions (PDFs) directly from data samples. The core of our approach involves encoding data into a quantum state and utilizing quantum gates to perform calculations related to the PDF. Furthermore, we address the challenges of noise inherent in quantum systems through the integration of quantum error correction techniques. This work lays the theoretical groundwork for a quantum-enhanced PDE method, demonstrating the feasibility of significantly improving estimation speed and accuracy for complex datasets. We focus on the conceptual design and potential benefits of this approach, without performing actual experimental validation.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Grey-Tail Rabbit Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTRA-SA), inspired by the foraging behavior of grey-tailed rabbits. GTRA-SA utilizes a dynamic population size adjustment mechanism based on the rabbit's perception of resource availability, and a novel adaptive inertia weight scheme influenced by the rabbit's responsiveness to environmental changes. The core of the algorithm lies in the 'leap' and 'scan' operations, which emulate the rabbit's ability to quickly adapt its search pattern. The algorithm's parameters are dynamically adjusted using a sigmoid function, reflecting the rabbit's behavioral changes based on local landscape evaluation. This approach aims to improve the convergence speed and robustness of the optimization process. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, underlying principles, and potential applications.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Differential Privacy for Graph Data
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum error correction (QEC) to enhance differential privacy (DP) for graph data. Traditional DP mechanisms, when applied to graph datasets, often result in substantial utility loss due to the inherent structure and complexity of graph representations. We propose a novel approach that utilizes QEC to mitigate this issue by providing a stronger level of privacy protection during computations performed on the graph. Our framework aims to balance privacy guarantees with data utility, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to safeguard sensitive information while enabling meaningful analysis. The core idea is that by detecting and correcting errors introduced during computations, we can significantly reduce the risk of information leakage, thus improving the overall privacy-utility trade-off. We present a theoretical analysis of the proposed method and outline a potential implementation strategy, highlighting the key challenges and future research directions. The primary contribution lies in exploring the feasibility and potential benefits of QEC within the context of DP for graph data, addressing a critical gap in existing privacy-preserving techniques.

title: Title: Based on Non-Linear Geometric Topology for Quantum System Control
abstract: Quantum systems pose significant challenges in achieving precise and stable control, particularly in complex environments. Traditional control algorithms often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability. This paper introduces a novel control algorithm leveraging the unique properties of non-linear geometric topology to address these challenges. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the system's geometry based on feedback, enabling more robust and responsive control. The core mechanism hinges on the inherent non-linearity within the geometric structure, which allows for inherent stability and precise manipulation. This approach offers a fundamentally new perspective on quantum system control, potentially unlocking advancements in precision measurement, quantum computation, and quantum information processing.

title: Acacia Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Acacia Rat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Acacia Rat, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of acacia rats. Acacia rats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the core principles of their navigation, resource selection, and memory mechanisms to create a robust and effective optimization process. Acacia Rat employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a unique memory structure mimicking the rat's spatial awareness. We present the algorithm's design, detailing the key parameters and operational rules. Furthermore, we evaluate Acacia Rat's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities and potential advantages over established metaheuristic methods. The results show that Acacia Rat performs well in both continuous and discrete optimization landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive memory and dynamic parameter adjustment contribute to its effectiveness. This research provides a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization and offers a valuable tool for solving complex real-world problems.

title: ## Deep-Sea Shrimp Inspired Adaptive Resonance Optimization Algorithm (DSARO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Deep-Sea Shrimp Inspired Adaptive Resonance Optimization Algorithm (DSARO), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique. The algorithm draws inspiration from the observed adaptive behaviors of deep-sea red shrimp, specifically their ability to navigate and forage in extremely low-visibility environments and their efficient resource utilization. DSARO leverages a dynamic population structure, adaptive resonance mechanisms, and a novel exploration-exploitation balance strategy, mimicking the shrimp's responses to environmental changes and resource availability. The core concept involves a population of 'shrimp' representing potential solutions, with each shrimp's 'position' in the search space continuously adjusted based on both local and global information. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the population size and the degree of resonance based on the overall search landscape. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, key components, and potential applications, aiming to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology Mapping and the Fusion of Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Dynamic Topology Mapping (DTM) offers a novel approach to quantum entanglement measurement, leveraging the inherent topological properties of the entangled state. This paper explores the development of a quantum entanglement measurement protocol based on DTM, demonstrating significant improvements in measurement precision and robustness against environmental noise. We introduce a dynamic mapping technique that models the evolution of entangled states as a topological transformation, optimizing the measurement process through the self-similarity inherent in the topology. This method provides a fundamentally different perspective on entanglement measurement, addressing limitations of traditional approaches.

title: A Study on the Copyright Infringement Liability of Generative AI Service Providers - Focusing on Output Stage Infringement Arising from Memorization and Legislative Proposals for Safe Harbor Provisions -
abstract: 생성형 AI 서비스제공자의 저작권 침해 책임은 학습단계의 복제와산출단계의 침해를 분리하여 파악하기 어렵다. 학습과정에서 형성된모델의 내부 상태가 산출물로 외부화되는 방식이 학습의 적법성, 산출물의 침해성 및 책임주체 판단을 연결하기 때문이다. 본 연구는 생성형 AI의 작동을 ‘확률적 모방성’, ‘초과 모방성’, ‘암기’, ‘재현’ 등의 개념으로 구분하고, 모델 내부의 암기가 저작권법상 복제에 해당하는 상황과 맥락을 검토한다. 암기는 모델의 학습방식, 데이터셋의 유형 및특성, 데이터 중복도, 프롬프트 및 디코딩 방식에 따라 편차를 보이는경험적 현상이자 정도의 문제이므로, 특정 저작물의 안정적ㆍ반복적재현 가능성을 중심으로 판단하여야 한다. 독일의 GEMA v. OpenAI 판결은 단순한 프롬프트에 의한 가사의 반복 재현을 근거로 모델 내부의 암기를 복제로 인정한 반면, 영국의Getty Images v. Stability AI 판결은 모델 가중치가 저작물의 사본이 아니라 학습된 패턴과 특징을 반영한다고 보아 침해복제물성을 부정하였다. 한국 저작권법상 복제와 고정의 개념도 모델 내부 복제라는 이론구성을 배제하지 않지만, 복제 개념의 과잉 확장을 방지하려면 안정적 ㆍ반복적 재현에 관한 엄격한 증명이 필요하다. 미국의 Bartz v. Anthropic 및 Kadrey v. Meta 판결 역시 학습단계의 공정이용을 판단하면서 산출단계에서 침해적 산출물의 부재와 시장대체 효과를 중시하였다. 책임주체는 프롬프트의 침해유발성, 암기와 재현의 정도 및 서비스제공자의 통제가능성에 따라 해당 여부를 판단하여야 한다. 이용자가원문 재현을 의도한 경우에는 이용자의 직접침해가 문제되고, 일반적인 프롬프트만으로 특정 저작물이 반복 재현되고 그 원인이 학습구조나 서비스 설계에 있는 경우에는 개발자 또는 서비스제공자의 책임이문제될 수 있다. RAG 결합 서비스는 외부 저작물을 직접 검색ㆍ투입한다는 점에서 모델 내부 암기와 구별하여 평가할 필요가 있다. 본 연구는 생성형 AI의 동적 산출구조에 맞추어 ‘통지 후 합리적 조치’를 내용으로 하는 책임제한 특례를 제안한다. 권리자가 저작물, 침해 산출물, 재현 프롬프트 및 침해 근거를 구체적으로 통지하면 서비스제공자는 프롬프트 필터ㆍ출력 필터와 검색대상 제외 등 합리적인조치를 취하는 것을 요건으로 한다. 다만 특정 저작물의 모방을 의도한 모델, 통지 후 반복 침해를 방치한 서비스 및 특정 저작물을 고의적으로 검색ㆍ재현하는 RAG형 서비스에는 동일한 면책을 인정하기 어렵다. 결국 생성형 AI의 저작권 침해 책임은 학습방식, 의도성, 재현가능성, 통제가능성 및 위험창출의 정도에 비례하여 배분되어야 한다.

title: XChondNet: Explainable Chondrogenic Tumor Diagnosis by Spatial-Context-Aware Synergistic Deep Feature Fusion
abstract: As a common benign bone tumor, the pathological diagnosis of chondrogenic tumors needs to accurately analyze the calcification pattern of the cartilage matrix, key spatial topology information, and other important indicators. However, chondrogenic tumors is a rare disease, doctors lack sufficient reference data and experience in diagnosis. At the same time, complex spatial structural information also increases the difficulty of diagnosis, which leads to inconsistencies in the diagnosis’s results of different doctors. In contrast, with the development of technology, artificial intelligence (AI) with its fast, accurate, and robust characteristics can effectively improve the efficiency and accuracy of diagnosis. However, the application of AI in this field is still unrecognized, so it is urgent to develop a model that can help doctors in diagnosis to improve accuracy and efficiency. In this study, we propose XChondNet, an explainable spatial-context-aware synergistic deep feature fusion model for WSI-based chondrogenic tumor classification. The model proposes a fusion mechanism of pathological and positional features so that the model can effectively perceive spatial structural information and a parallel classifier mechanism based on potential coding, which can effectively solve the problem of class imbalance in chondrogenic tumors data. We evaluated the XChondNet model on our chondrogenic tumors dataset and the experimental results verified its effectiveness in the classification of the chondrogenic tumors subtype. In the test phase, compared to the other advanced models, the XChondNet model achieved state-of-the-art accuracy (ACC), area under the curve (AUC), F1 score and Recall rate. And the XChondNet model explicitly reflects the consistency with pathologists’ concerns, which improves the interpretability of AI.

title: A typology of customer resistance factors toward hotel service automation and their structural effects: a CONCOR and QAP analysis of online reviews
abstract: 환대산업의 디지털 전환이 가속되며 hospitality revolution 4.0이 본격화했지만, 선행연구는 기술 수용을 전제로 한 친혁신 편향에 치우쳐 고객 저항 현상을 체계적으로 다루지 못하였다. 또한 4차 산업혁명 이전에 정립된 저항 요인으로 자동화 환경에서 새롭게 출현하는 저항 신호를 충분히 설명하기 어렵다는 한계가 있다. 이에 본 연구는 hospitality revolution 4.0의 특성이 반영된 고객 저항 요인을 온라인 리뷰를 활용하여 도출하고, 도출된 요인이 고객 저항 형성에 미치는 구조적 영향을 실증적으로 규명하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 2020년부터 2024년까지 TripAdvisor 및 Google Review에 게시된 국내 호텔 리뷰 중 서비스 자동화 관련 경험이 명시적으로 언급된 리뷰 15,847건을 수집 및 정제한 뒤 TF-IDF 가중치 기반 핵심 키워드 50개를 선정하였다. 선정된 핵심 키워드는 연결중심성 및 위세중심성 분석, CONCOR 군집화, QAP 상관분석, QAP 회귀분석을 수행하여 분석하였다. 분석 결과에 따르면 고객 저항 요인은 기술 운용 결함, 자동화 기반 환대 결손, 서비스 절차 부정합, 자동화 수용 유보의 네 가지 유형으로 도출되었다. 회귀 모형에서는 기술 운용 결함이 고객 저항 형성에 가장 강한 구조적 관계가 확인되었으며 자동화 기반 환대 결손과 서비스 절차 부정합 역시 유의한 정(+)의 구조적 관계가 밝혀졌다. 그러나 자동화 수용 유보는 통계적으로 유의한 구조적 관계를 보이지 않아 변화 자체에 대한 거리감이 곧바로 저항 행동을 구성하지 않음을 확인하였다. 본 연구는 능동적 저항과 수동적 저항을 통합적으로 검증하며 새로운 분석 차원을 제시함으로써 혁신 저항 이론의 외연을 확장하였다. 또한 호텔 실무자에게는 자동화 시스템의 운용 안정성 강화, 하이브리드 응대 모델 구축, 절차 표준화라는 실천적 관리 방향을 제시하였다.

title: Benchmarking Peptide-Protein Affinity Prediction Across Peptide and Target Shifts
abstract: Peptide-protein affinity models are often evaluated with a single data split, obscuring whether they interpolate among measurements for observed targets or generalize across peptide or target shifts. We integrated three sources of quantitative peptide-protein binding data to obtain 11,349 deduplicated pairs and benchmarked ten peptide representations, ESM-2 protein embeddings, and six regressors under peptide-similarity, within-target, and leave-target-out partitions. Across 60 matched representation-regressor configurations, mean test Spearman correlations were 0.462, 0.669, and 0.530, respectively. The top configuration shifted from ECFP-16 count fingerprints with random forest in the first two settings to HELM-BERT with Extra Trees when exact target sequences were excluded. Representation-rank correlations ranged from -0.042 to 0.624 across partitions, whereas regressor-rank correlations ranged from 0.771 to 0.943. Learning curves showed that representation differences were largest with limited supervision and narrowed as training data increased. PeptideCLM-2 adaptation and simple element-wise interaction features provided no consistent gain over a frozen encoder and direct concatenation under the tested protocols. These conclusions are specific to a dataset that pools transformed Kd, Ki, and IC50 measurements and to target exclusion at the exact-sequence level. Peptide-protein affinity benchmarks should therefore align data partitions with the intended use and jointly assess the effects of data scale, molecular representation, and downstream learner.

title: Multi-instance Learning as Downstream Task of Self-Supervised Learningbased Pre-trained Model
abstract: Multi-instance learning (MIL) is a type of weakly supervised learning. In MIL, a set of instances is defined asa bag, and only bag labels are known. In recent years, deep learning-based MIL has been applied in medical imaging,especially in histopathological images. However, when classifying the marker in the brain hematoma CT imageswhich we deal with, simply applying MIL leads to spurious correlations. In addition, many studies applying MIL tohistopathological images handle thousands of instances per bag and show high performance, while our task strugglesto learn with a few hundred instances per bag and has low performance. In this paper, we address these problems. Wepropose using a pre-trained model with self-supervised learning for the multi-instance learner as a downstream task.We apply self-supervised learning to the instance feature extractor in MIL to learn effective feature representations ofpatch images. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves improvements of 6.5% in accuracy and11.2% in the F1-score without falling into the spurious correlation problem.

title: A Multi-Layer Cryptographic Framework for Resource-Constrained IoMT Devices Using Constructive Research Technique
abstract: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices frequently lack sufficient computational power, memory and energy resources. IoMT systems often require real-time data processing and transmission, as well as a comprehensive key management infrastructure to guarantee the security and integrity of encryption keys. Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices can benefit from hardware-based security features such as secure enclaves, trusted execution environments and hardware-backed key storage to improve the overall security of cryptographic applications. Choosing methods that can take advantage of these hardware-based security characteristics while reducing computational power and memory consumption in real-time data processing can improve IoMT performance and security. This study suggested a multi-layer cryptography system for resource-constrained IoMT devices. This projected security framework encrypts and hashes IoMT data at the physical layer using AES 256, Trivium, and HMAC SHA256. The AES-256 is used to encrypt critical data that requires higher levels of security, such as IoMT data. The TRIVIUM approach, is used for real-time data encryption when low latency and efficiency are crucial, but the HMAC SHA256 is utilized to guarantee data integrity and authenticity. This work uses the constructive research technique, which is appropriate for investigating elements of digital preservation. The constructive research technique allows academics to create a model that was utilized to solve the challenge of data security in IoMT. The system was created using the Python programming language.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm for quantum machine learning models, designed to enhance model generalization and learning efficiency through adaptive parameter optimization guided by training data features. Traditional quantum machine learning approaches often rely on static parameter settings, limiting the model's capacity to fully exploit the intricacies of the data. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts model parameters in response to training data characteristics, leading to improved performance across a range of tasks. We introduce the concept of "dynamic parameter adjustment" to facilitate this adaptive optimization process. This work offers a promising approach to overcome the limitations of static parameter tuning in quantum machine learning, potentially unlocking new capabilities in complex datasets.

title: Nonlinear Multi-Body Synchronization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Nonlinear Multi-Body Synchronization Algorithm (NMBSA) that leverages quantum entanglement to achieve precise synchronization of multiple microscopic particles, such as electrons and atoms. Traditional synchronization methods rely on classical communication, posing significant challenges for quantum systems. This algorithm employs quantum entanglement to facilitate a more efficient and secure synchronization process. The core mechanism involves the instantaneous correlation of entangled states, enabling the algorithm to predict and precisely synchronize the quantum states of the particles. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum principles, and its potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing synchronization techniques.

title: Quantum Information Encoding and Reconstruction of Memory
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum information theory to address fundamental questions surrounding memory. The core claim posits that memory, at its essence, can be encoded as quantum information, and that quantum information processing techniques can be leveraged to achieve memory reconstruction and enhancement. The proposed mechanism centers around the exploitation of quantum entanglement and superposition, leading to a novel quantum memory storage and reconstruction model. This work introduces a theoretical framework that bridges the gap between quantum mechanics and neuroscience, exploring a fundamentally new approach to memory storage and retrieval. The paper details the key concepts, mathematical formulations, and potential implications of this paradigm shift. We propose a model where memories are represented as quantum states, manipulated through quantum gates, and subsequently reconstructed with enhanced fidelity. The central focus is on developing a quantifiable method for encoding and manipulating memories, opening doors for potential therapeutic applications and a deeper understanding of the human brain. ---

title: Physics Simulation of Quantum Entanglement Optimization – Optimization of Quantum Entanglement States
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in which two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, holds immense promise for quantum computing and quantum information processing. However, harnessing entanglement effectively requires precise control over its quantum states. This paper explores the application of physics simulation techniques to optimize quantum entanglement states, specifically focusing on a novel geometric optimization method leveraging the unique properties of entanglement. Traditional optimization methods struggle to fully capture the intricacies of entangled states, necessitating a shift towards a more sophisticated approach. We propose a new method that utilizes entanglement to guide the search for optimal quantum states, resulting in enhanced efficiency and control over quantum computation. The core claim is that this method provides a significant improvement in the performance of quantum algorithms by effectively manipulating entangled states. The mechanism involves the exploitation of entanglement's non-classical correlation to generate a more complex and structured quantum state, facilitating faster and more accurate computations. This research presents a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Self-Adaptive Probability Field Theory Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-adaptive probability field theory optimization to enhance the dynamic computational capabilities of probability field theories. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter adjustments, while this approach offers the potential for automated structural optimization, leading to significant improvements in data analysis and machine learning. We propose a novel methodology that dynamically adjusts probability field parameter values based on a learned, self-adaptive structure, resulting in a more robust and efficient probabilistic model. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this technique through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing enhanced computational performance and improved data representation. The core claim is that self-adaptive probability field theory optimization leads to a substantial increase in the dynamic calculation capabilities of probability field theories.
